summary: This commit lands the HOLD_FOR_OWNER_SIGNOFF mechanism (real marker line parsed from EXPECTED_OUTPUT/CONSTRAINTS, threaded through task-gateway.py -> veridian-task.py -> task.yaml -> supervisor-entrypoint.sh's merge-decision block) fixing the PR563 incident where a prose-only hold instruction was silently ignored by the auto-merge pipeline, plus a corrected veridian-task.py checkpoint state machine and real-branch resolution fix. Independently verified rather than trusting the self-report: both new files pass py_compile/bash -n; both new pytest files (hold_for_signoff_test.py, veridian_task_branch_resolution_test.py) pass against the real shipped code, as do three pre-existing supervisor shell tests that exercise the same supervisor-entrypoint.sh file; risk-tier.py itself independently classifies this diff as tier1; no .github/workflows/** files are touched; no hardcoded secrets are present; and the unset CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN/ANTHROPIC_API_KEY/ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL block exactly mirrors the already-established, working pattern in worker-entrypoint.sh (clearing a stale .env value so the real ~/.claude Max-subscription session credentials are used), not a bug. The hold-for-signoff gate is correctly positioned to override tier/verdict within the final merge-decision if/elif chain, and merge-success is judged by a fresh gh pr view state check rather than a shell exit code, consistent with this codebase's own documented incident fixes.
